title: Prefill-phase-aware kernel weighting scaler for mixed-prefill/decode workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a lightweight kernel weighting scaler that dynamically biases kernel selection during the prefill phase vs decode phase. The goal is to reduce latency tail and cost regressions for mixed workloads where prefill length distribution and decode stochasticity make a static kernel policy suboptimal. This ticket covers the estimator, gating logic, telemetry instrumentation, offline profiling datasets, and a canary rollout plan for ded-1 and hosted clusters.
acceptance_criteria: New kernel weighting scaler integrated with kernel-picker API and configurable via runtime-config
<=5% p95 latency regression on canonical workloads compared to current policy, and >=3% median cost improvement for short-prefill-heavy traffic
Telemetry surfaces per-phase kernel choice distribution and a channel for automatic rollback when latency SLO violation > 1.5x for 15m
E2E tests cover seqlen buckets (0-32,33-128,129-512,>512) and prefill/decode mix scenarios
Feature flag + rollout plan validated on dedicated cluster with synthetic traffic before host rollout
design_notes: Rationale: static kernel heuristics assume a single traffic shape. Prefill introduces a deterministic long prefix cost surface; decode phase benefits from low-latency small-kernel paths. We need a phase-aware scaler that shifts preference without full model switching.

Scoring model: combine an architecture-aware cost prior (per-GPU, per-kernel microbenchmarks) with an online seqlen histogram and a phase confidence score. Output is a weight multiplier applied to kernel scores before argmax selection.

Phase detection: infer prefill vs decode via request metadata where available (is_prefill flag), otherwise use tokens_left / request_length heuristics with conservative default to avoid misclassification.
Config knobs: scaling_floor, scaling_ceiling, decay_time_ms (how quickly weights revert post-prefill), seqlen_bucket_weights, and architecture overrides (NVidia A100 vs H100 vs AMD MI250).
Fallback: when telemetry is missing or weighter emits NaN, revert to baseline kernel selection to guarantee safety.
implementation_notes: Add 'phase_score' output to request feature extractor (runtime/features) and expose to kernel-picker interface (internal API change RFC #327)
Implement lightweight weighter that reads static microbench table (from build-time JSON) and online seqlen histogram; perform multiplication in FP16 to keep CPU overhead low
Create microbench harness to capture per-kernel cost for representative seqlen slices and key GPU types. Store results in /artifacts/kernel-microbench/2026-02-06
Instrument telemetry (metrics: kernel_choice_by_phase, kernel_weight_multiplier, phase_confusion_rate) and add Grafana dashboard panels (dashboard id: runtime-kernel-weighter-v1)
Add integration tests in runtime-integration that assert selection invariants for mocked microbench inputs (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2138)
Ensure compatibility with existing warmstart/warmup heuristics (see ENG-712908) and use dependency signals to avoid conflicting warmstart overrides
testing_plan: Unit: weighter math, seed determinism, edge cases (zero-cost kernel, missing microbench)
Integration: inject synthetic seqlen traces into local runtime and assert kernel distribution shifts between prefill/decode requests
Performance: run dedicated microbench cluster jobs to measure CPU overhead of weighter (target <1% CPU for 99th), and validate p50/p95 token latency under mixed load
Canary: staged rollout on dedicated GPU pool ded-1 for 48 hours with traffic mirror of 5% before host-wide rollout
Chaos: simulate misclassification (prefill labeled as decode and vice versa) and confirm fallback behavior and minimal SLA impact
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind runtime-config and env var RUNTIME_KERNEL_WEIGHTER=canary
Step 1: internal canary on staging with synthetic workloads (2026-03-03 to 2026-03-05)
Step 2: 5% traffic mirror on ded-1 for 48 hours, monitor kernel_choice_by_phase and latency SLOs (2026-03-06 to 2026-03-08)
Step 3: 25% rollout if telemetry stable for 24h, 50% after 48h, full rollout after 7 days with automated rollback trigger
Rollback criteria: any regression > 10% p95 latency or customer-facing error increase > 0.1% over baseline
risks: Misclassification of phase causing worse kernel choices (mitigation: conservative decay_time and canary testing)
Telemetry overhead and cardinality explosion if we introduce too-fine-grained per-kernel metrics (mitigation: aggregate to buckets and cap labels)
Interference with existing warmstart and kernel warm caches (mitigation: coordinate with ENG-712908 and add compatibility layer)
Model drift where offline microbench no longer reflects hardware after driver updates (mitigation: periodic microbench job in CI and build-time artifacts updated weekly)
Edge platforms (on-prem customers) without phase metadata might see suboptimal behavior; provide opt-out via runtime-config
progress_updates: 2026-02-17: Spike complete — validated that a multiplicative weighter can reduce selection churn in simulator. Prototype in runtime/experimental/phase-weighter branch.
2026-02-22: Microbench harness results uploaded: /artifacts/kernel-microbench/2026-02-06. H100 shows 12% median advantage for kernel K7 on 1-32 token decode; A100 prefers K3 for >256 tokens.

2026-02-28: API RFC posted for small kernel-picker change (RFC #327). Design review requested from infra and runtime teams. Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/runtime/Prefill+Phase+Kernel+Weighter
2026-03-01: Initial implementation merged behind feature flag to staging (PR #2138). Added metrics and basic unit tests. CPU overhead measured at ~0.6% in local perf run.

2026-03-02: Observability panels configured; started internal canary on staging. Noted a spike in phase_confusion_rate for HTTP proxied requests — debugging network metadata loss with edge-proxy team. Assigned to @Sofia Reyes for edge metadata fix (ENG-916010)
